Create a fully functional, minimalistic Sudoku web app with a calm, elegant, mobile-first design.
Use soft colors, smooth animations, rounded corners, and clean typography.
The app flow consists of 4 main screens: Difficulty Selection → Level Grid → Game Screen → Settings.

GENERAL DESIGN REQUIREMENTS

Ultra-minimalistic UI, Zen-inspired.

Color palette: whites, off-whites, very soft beige and light gray.

Rounded corners everywhere.

Soft grid lines.

Subtle animations (fade, slight scale, slide transitions).

Geometric modern font.

Buttons and interactive elements should feel airy, spacious, and easy to tap on mobile.

APP STRUCTURE
1. Splash / Welcome Screen

App name at center: “Minimal Sudoku”

Subtle fade-in animation

After 1.5 seconds, automatically navigate to Difficulty Selection Screen

2. Difficulty Selection Screen

Create a clean screen containing 6 large cards or buttons, arranged in 2 columns:

Difficulties:

Super Easy

Easy

Normal

Hard

Intense

Impossible

Behaviors & Design:

Each card has a title + small description (placeholder).

On click → navigate to the Level Selection Screen for that difficulty.

Add a minimal top-right settings icon (gear) to open the Settings screen.

3. Level Selection Screen (per difficulty)

This screen displays 30 levels arranged in a 6×5 grid (or flexible responsive grid).

Each level is represented by a small rounded square button with:

Level number

State styling:

Not started: bright, active

In progress: small “•” indicator or subtle badge

Completed: dimmed or faded style (like the “light is off”), OR a small checkmark

Features:

Title at top: "[Difficulty Name] – Select Level"

Progress indicator: “X / 30 levels completed”

Back button (top left): returns to Difficulty Selection

If the player left an unfinished level, show a banner:

“Continue Level 7”

Clicking it loads the ongoing game with timer resuming

4. Game Screen

This screen contains the Sudoku board and all game controls.

A. Header

Difficulty (ex: “Normal”)

Timer (counts while playing; stops when leaving the screen)

Reset Level button

Pause button

Settings icon

B. Sudoku Grid

9×9 grid

Soft light borders

Highlight:

Selected cell

Selected row

Selected column

Selected 3×3 block

Pre-filled numbers are darker and non-editable.

User-input numbers slightly bolder or different shade.

Notes appear in small, subtle font inside the cell.

C. Controls Section

Below the board, include:

Top row of controls:

Undo

Pencil Mode (toggle notes)

Erase

(Optional) Hint button (can be empty function)

Bottom row: number pad:

Buttons 1–9

Rounded squares, minimalistic styling

When Pencil Mode is ON, numbers become notes

D. Pause State

When paused:

Show a blurred overlay screen

Buttons:

Resume

Restart Level

Back to Levels

5. Game Completion

When a puzzle is solved:

Fade-in modal overlay

Title: “Puzzle Completed!”

Buttons:

“Next Level”

“Back to Level List”

Update local storage:

Mark level as completed

Clear saved progress for that level

6. Settings Screen

A minimal full-screen modal with rounded top corners.

Include toggles for:

Music ON/OFF

Sound effects ON/OFF

Highlight mode ON/OFF

Auto-notes ON/OFF (optional)

Button: Reset App Progress (confirmation modal required)

Settings must persist in local storage.

GAME LOGIC REQUIREMENTS

Implement a Sudoku puzzle generator OR load preset puzzles for each difficulty (placeholders allowed).

Each difficulty has 30 puzzles.

Auto-save board progress, notes, and timer state on:

Leaving the game screen

Switching tabs

Navigating back

Auto-load progress when returning to that level.

Timer stops when user leaves game or pauses.

Validate moves (visually highlight conflicts).

Disable editing of preset cells.

DATA PERSISTENCE

Use local storage to save:

Per difficulty:

Completed levels

Levels in progress

Stored board state

Stored notes

Global:

Sound settings

Music settings

Highlight mode

Auto-notes setting

ANIMATIONS

Button press: soft scale-down

Screen transitions: fade or slide

When solving puzzle: celebrate with soft fade and scale

RESPONSIVE REQUIREMENTS

Entire UI must look perfect on mobile-first.

On desktop: center the content with max width and larger spacing.

Use flexible units so the grid always fits nicely.

IMPORTANT

The final result should feel like a premium, minimalist Sudoku app similar to the style of:

iOS apps

Calm / Zen productivity apps

Avoid clutter. Prioritize clarity, elegance, and comfort.

DELIVERABLE

A fully working Sudoku app with:

Navigation

Persistent levels

30 puzzles per difficulty (placeholder ok)

Fully functional UI and interactions

Minimalistic, premium look

**Developing the Framework**

I've been dissecting the user's request, zeroing in on the core goal: a sleek, minimalist Sudoku web app with a Zen aesthetic. The tech stack is clear: React 18+, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, local storage, and Phosphor Icons are the pillars. Initial conceptualization focuses on the component structure, prioritizing reusability and maintainability. I'm exploring efficient state management within React components.


**Mapping the Feature Set**

I'm now concretizing the feature set, favoring Lucide for icons and a soft color palette with rounded corners for the visual style. The core user flow is defined.  I've detailed the 6 difficulties, 30 levels per difficulty, and game features like undo, pencil mode, timer, autosave, and conflict highlighting. Local storage will handle *all* data persistence. I'm considering using an existing Sudoku generator for valid puzzles. I'm also planning the directory structure.


**Refining the Structure**

My focus is now firmly on the directory structure. I've broken down the components into logical groups: `layout`, `screens`, `ui`, and `game`. Within `utils`, `sudoku.ts` will handle puzzle generation and validation, while `storage.ts` provides local storage wrappers.  I'm also solidifying the core types: `Cell`, `Board`, `Difficulty`, and `GameState`, which will be crucial for the application. The goal is to build a robust and well-organized foundation.


**Integrating Navigation & Views**

I'm now fully immersed in the application's flow. I've realized `react-router` is essential for handling views within this single-page app and I can manage screens with a global state. I'm focusing on the implementation details now: Splash (simple `useEffect`), Difficulty Select (cards), Level Select (buttons with storage-based status), Game (complex state with board, notes, timer, etc.), and a settings modal. Tailwind's color palette is taking shape with backgrounds (`bg-stone-50` or `bg-[#fcfbf9]`), text (`text-stone-800`), and accents like `bg-stone-200`. I'm starting to sketch out the sudoku logic for puzzle generation and saving game state.


**Solidifying Game Logic**

I'm now diving deep into the game's core mechanics. I'm nailing down the data structures and how game state will be managed: `Board`, `Cell` and the conflict logic.  I'm focusing on the `handleNumberInput(num)` function, which will manage preset cells, notes, and value assignment, including conflict detection. I'm also implementing the timer using `useEffect` with `setInterval` and considering pausing on screen change or user pause.


**Consolidating the Application**

I've been working on the app's structure to minimize XML overhead. I've decided to keep `App.tsx` manageable by moving the game screen logic to `SudokuGame.tsx`. This keeps things organized. I'm focusing on the core components and their interactions, and how the state will flow through each. I'm also planning the grid structure and overall mounting. I'm now exploring Sudoku generation specifics.


**Finalizing the Details**

I'm now prioritizing the application's polish and user experience. I've opted for CSS animations for the win state celebration to maintain a lightweight dependency profile. I'm focusing on "back" navigation and timer persistence, ensuring smooth transitions and data integrity. I'm also carefully refining the visual style, paying close attention to grid line aesthetics and color balance for an aesthetically pleasing and usable interface. Lucide icons are in place for key actions, and I'm ensuring everything is wired correctly.


**Prioritizing Implementation**

I'm now fully immersed in coding. My color scheme is finalized: backgrounds will feature a warm white/beige (`#f9f8f6`), primary text will use `text-stone-800`, and accents will be `bg-stone-800`. Selected cells will use `bg-blue-100`, while the same number highlighting will use `bg-blue-200`. I'm focusing on crafting the level generation using the seed/level index. Rather than generating *unique* boards on the fly (which risks performance bottlenecks), I'll use a seeded random generator so Level 1 always generates the same board given the same code logic. I'm focusing on the *how* of the code.

Using `number | null` directly is valid for a strict browser context, but `any` might suppress errors, so I'll go with `ReturnType<typeof setInterval>`. I also increased the z-index of the Settings Modal to `z-[999]` and adjusted its backdrop opacity to ensure it clearly overlays everything behind it.
